title: Mouse without borders says keys dont match, when it does
author: Jebarson
summary: Mouse Without Borders rejects cross-version pairing as InvalidKey; a second user reproduced the 0.100-to-0.101 mismatch and confirmed that updating the older peer resolves it.

status.label: Resolved by matching peer versions
status.detail: A corroborating user reports that pairing succeeds after updating the older PowerToys installation.

next_action.label: Post matching-version guidance
next_action.reason: Document the confirmed recovery and avoid requesting diagnostics unless the failure persists with both peers current.

judgment.rationale: The original report’s strongest confounder was version skew. A second user reproduced the same cross-version failure and then confirmed that updating the older peer resolves the connection, matching Mouse Without Borders code that explicitly warns same-version peers are required when handshake/clipboard connections are rejected.
evidence: One machine runs PowerToys 0.101.2362.0 and the other runs 0.100.0.0.
The newer machine restored a backup originating from the 0.100.0.0 machine.
The supplied status text records the remote peer as InvalidKey.
A second user reproduced the failure between PowerToys 0.100.2 and 0.101.2362.
That user reports the connection works after updating the older installation.
MouseWithoutBorders/App/Core/Clipboard.cs shows rejected connections surface “Make sure you run the same version in all machines.”
judgment.recommended_action: Advise updating both peers to the same current PowerToys version and only collect paired diagnostics if InvalidKey persists afterward.

issue_context.summary: Cross-version Mouse Without Borders peers can report InvalidKey even when the visible key matches, and updating the older peer has resolved the reported scenario.
known_information: Settings from the older installation were restored on the newer machine.
The reporter manually copied the displayed key.
The supplied status output identifies the remote peer and records InvalidKey.
A corroborating user reports that the same version-skew failure is resolved by updating the older machine.
inferences: The confirmed matching-version recovery makes a current same-version key-comparison defect less likely.
The failure may be caused by protocol or serialized-state differences across the 0.100-to-0.101 boundary.
issue_context.analysis: The new comment supplies the controlled outcome the earlier action requested: cross-version pairing fails and updating resolves it. The dashboard should expose matching-version guidance rather than a stale diagnostic request.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the full live issue body, the single comment, labels, assignees, timeline, and closed-by-PR references.
Searched current issues for InvalidKey/key mismatch wording and found no stronger duplicate than the live corroborating comment.
Inspected Mouse Without Borders connection-handshake messaging, which already tells users to run the same version on all machines when a connection is rejected.

actions.label: Post matching-version MWB guidance

comment.body: Thanks for the peer and status details. The additional report confirms that Mouse Without Borders can reject pairing when the machines use PowerToys 0.100.x and 0.101.x, and that the connection works after updating the older installation. Please update both machines to the same current PowerToys version and pair again with a newly generated key. If `InvalidKey` still occurs with both peers current, immediately submit `/bugreport` from each machine and attach both ZIP files, identifying which came from each peer.
